Ericsson Cradlepoint · NCOS SDK sample

NCX self-provision

Staging a fleet of Ericsson Cradlepoint routers means licenses, sites, resources, and group moves for every one. With this app, you drop routers into a staging group and each one provisions itself to Ericsson NetCloud Exchange (NCX) in 10 automatic steps, then moves itself to production.

Zero touch

Move a router into the staging group. No one logs in to it.

More info
Move devices in batches of up to 50. Each router works through the steps on its own and logs progress as "[Step X/10]" in its system log.

Set up once, applied to all

A short wizard on your computer sets the staging group. An optional CSV adds per-router details.

More info
The wizard validates your keys and settings, then writes them to the staging group's SDK Data. In the CSV, a router's row is matched by its Ericsson NetCloud Manager router ID.

Picks up where it left off

Progress is saved after each step, so a failure or reboot doesn't mean starting over.

More info
Completed steps are skipped on a re-run. Transient API failures are retried up to 3 times, with a growing delay between tries.

One router, start to finish

Press Play walkthrough for a guided tour, or move a router into staging yourself.
Waiting in the box
    Router system log
    No activity yet. The app starts when the router lands in the staging group.
    What each step does
    • 1 to 3. Wait for uptime and a WAN connection, load the API keys from the router's certificates, then check readiness. Firmware must match the production group, checked every 15 seconds for up to an hour.
    • 4. Optional. Fill the config template from the router's CSV row, and set its description and custom fields.
    • 5. Apply the Secure Connect license, plus SD-WAN, HMF, and AI licenses if chosen.
    • 6. Create the exchange site, with tags and DNS settings.
    • 7. Optional. Delete the resources NCX creates automatically with a new site.
    • 8. Create your resources: the LAN subnet, host name, and wildcard domain, plus any extras from the CSV.
    • 9. Optional. Set up DNS force redirect once the VPN tunnel is up.
    • 10. Move the router to the production group and clear its saved progress.

    How it works

    The big ideas, without the settings. Open any card for more.

    The staging group is the trigger

    The app is assigned to the staging group, so it only runs on routers placed there.

    More info
    The app reads its settings and API keys from the staging group's SDK Data and certificates. Nothing is typed on the router.

    The wizard does the setup

    Six pages on your computer collect keys, groups, license, and options, and check them before applying.

    More info
    API keys, groups, exchange network, and license are required. Optional pages cover add-on licenses, resources, tags, and bulk configuration. The last page reviews everything before it applies.

    Each router gets its own details

    Add a CSV and a config template, and each router picks up its own name, IP, tags, and more.

    More info
    The CSV needs one column, id, the router's NetCloud Manager ID. Other columns fill {{placeholders}} in the template. Without a CSV row, the router keeps its current name and LAN IP.

    Safe to re-run

    Finished steps are remembered and skipped, and secrets are kept out of the logs.

    More info
    After a successful move, the app clears its saved progress. If a step fails, the log says so and the saved progress is kept for the next run.

    See it in the app

    The staging wizard runs on your computer. Select a tile to enlarge it.

    SDK Data settings

    The wizard writes these to the staging group for you, and that's the recommended way to set them. Values are text, such as True or False.

    SettingRequiredDefaultWhat it does
    staging_group_idYesNoneNetCloud Manager group where routers wait to be provisioned.
    prod_group_idYesNoneGroup the router moves to when provisioning finishes.
    exchange_network_idYesNoneThe NCX or SASE exchange network the site is created in.
    secure_connect_licYesNoneSecure Connect license to apply, such as NCX-SC.
    lan_as_dnsNoFalseUse the router's primary LAN as the DNS server for the site. Needs local_domain when True.
    self_bulk_configNoOffSet to True to fill the config template from the router's CSV row.
    create_lan_resourceNoOffSet to True to create the primary LAN subnet resource.
    delete_auto_resourcesNoOffSet to True to delete the resources NCX creates with a new site.
    More settings
    • local_domain, primary_dns, secondary_dns: domain and custom DNS servers for the site. Custom DNS and LAN as DNS are mutually exclusive.
    • sdwan_lic, hmf_lic, ai_lic: optional add-on licenses.
    • create_cp_host_resource, create_wildcard_resource: host name and wildcard domain resources. These need LAN as DNS or custom DNS.
    • site_tags, lan_resource_tags, cp_host_tags, wildcard_tags: global tags, separated by commas or semicolons. Each tag is at least 2 characters, lowercase letters and numbers only.
    • bulk_config_file, config_template_file: default to router_grid.csv and config_template.json.
    • disable_force_dns: turn off DNS force redirect for all routers. A CSV column can override it per router.
    • Run the wizard first. It needs Python 3.8 or later and the packages in requirements.txt. It opens at http://localhost:8000 on your computer. The app itself has no web page on the router.
    • Then build the package, upload it in Ericsson NetCloud Manager under Tools, then SDK, and assign it to the staging group.
    • You need NetCloud Manager API v2 and v3 keys, a staging group, a production group, and an NCX or SASE exchange network.
    • Both groups should run compatible firmware. The router waits for firmware to match before it continues.
    • Move no more than 50 routers into staging at a time.
